title: OpenBrick3D joint table
description: standards/joints-*.json (kind joints): how the clip, hinge, ball and bar primitives of the LDraw Parts Library turn into connectors (docs/plan/07 section 3, the Q04 report's calibration table). Each entry is a fact about one primitive in its own frame, derived from its own geometry by scripts/derive-joint-table.py and cited. Read by openbrick-catalog as JointTable.

library.description: The library release the table was derived from, with the release file's SHA-256.

bars.description: The rule that finds bars, which have no primitive: a cylinder of this radius at least this long, in a part whose description holds one of the words.

primitive.description: The primitive's file name without .dat, lower case.

kind.description: The connector kind an instance makes.

axis.description: The joint's axis in the primitive's frame: a positive lattice axis.

origin.description: A point on that axis in the primitive's frame, LDU.

evidence.description: The primitive geometry the entry was read from.

knownFields.description: The fields schema 1.0 names, object by object; true means the value is checked by the main schema. Applied only to 1.0 documents (see atThisMinor), where any other field is an error.

atThisMinor.description: Matches a document whose pragma names a minor version this schema knows, 1.0 (or a patch of it). Such a document may use only the fields this schema names ($defs/knownFields). A document of a later 1.x minor may carry fields added since; this schema checks the fields it knows and ignores the rest, so older tools can still read newer minors (docs/plan/08 section 9). Unlike the other shared definitions this one follows the schema's own minor version (cargo xtask data checks it against $id).

pragma.description: Schema version pragma: major 1 and a minor, optionally a patch (docs/plan/08 sections 1 and 9). Every 1.x is accepted: readers ignore fields from minors newer than they know, and this schema checks only the fields it names in documents newer than 1.0 (see atThisMinor).

credit.description: Who made the document. Keeping it is a community norm, not a legal condition (LICENSE-POLICY.md).

profileId.description: A profile id: lower-case words joined by hyphens, where a word may hold dots, as in fdm-0.4 or resin-msla (docs/plan/05 section 3).
